title: Cross-center prediction of ICU-acquired weakness from early admission data
summary: In three Shanghai medical centers, five models predicted ICU-acquired weakness among 535 critically ill patients using variables available within 48 hours of admission. External AUROC was 0.853 for SVM and 0.841 for logistic regression; tree-based models showed overfitting. Model-guided care and improved patient outcomes were not tested.
ai_technology: Logistic regression, random forest, SVM, CART and XGBoost trained on early ICU clinical variables
organization: Shanghai General Hospital, Shanghai Jiao Tong University

evidence.tested: Five machine-learning algorithms and logistic regression were compared in 395 internal-cohort patients and externally validated in 140 patients from two other centers. External AUROC was 0.853 for SVM and 0.841 for logistic regression; tree-based methods showed substantial performance attenuation consistent with overfitting.
evidence.unknown: The study did not test whether model-guided care reduces ICU-acquired weakness or improves recovery; prospective interventional evaluation is still needed.
evidence.ai_role: Five predictive algorithms were trained with 10-fold cross-validated grid search on data available within 48 hours of admission; a six-predictor logistic model was also converted to a nomogram.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
